target_customer: Military headquarters and staffs (US Army, Air Force, Marine Corps, NATO allies) that plan operations
problem: Military staffs plan with slide decks and email, which is slow and keeps plans out of sync. Onebrief turns inputs into reusable building blocks and keeps planning products synchronized.
business_model: B2G enterprise SaaS sold through defense contracts

founders.name: Grant Demaree
prior_employers: US Army (5 years as an officer)
education: US Military Academy at West Point, Nuclear Engineering and International Relations
founders.background_notes: YC page: served on Army counter-Ebola efforts in Liberia and counter-ISIS campaign in Iraq. Only founder listed there; CB Insights says the company was formerly Broadcouncil.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time collaborative document sync with security accreditation for government networks. Hard parts are accreditation and data models for plans, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Government accreditation, program of record contracts and plan data held across commands create lock in. Palantir is cited as the main risk of building or buying planning software.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Through 2026 Onebrief works alongside Palantir and Anduril in the Army NGC2 environment per Interesting Engineering and won Army enterprise contracts in September 2025. No source shows an incumbent copying it away.

market_need_then: The YC description says military planning relies on PowerPoint and slow multi stakeholder processes. Company careers pages say slide workflows without version control tie up staffs for weeks or months.

branding.domain_note: Uses onebrief.com. CB Insights says it was formerly known as Broadcouncil (undated).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission focused and professional, aimed at defense buyers

rebrands.why: not stated in the source found (CB Insights)

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage of valuation and Army contracts built name recognition in defense, but no source discusses the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Onebrief was founded in 2019 by a former Army officer and joined YC in Summer 2021. It won Army and Air Force work and raised a Series B in 2024, a Series C in January 2025 at 650M, a 20M extension at 1.1B in June 2025 and a 200M Series D at 2.15B in January 2026 while buying Battle Road Digital. Founder domain insight, accreditation and a defense AI funding wave drove the growth.
notes: Series B: pulse2 (Sept 1, 2024) says the round brought total to 53M without stating the round size, so amount is null; Seedtable gives a Series B in August 2024 and a 335M valuation (aggregator, unverified). Series C: Insight Partners and Business Wire titles say total raised 103M, which with 53M implies 50M, and one outlet says 50M; 650M valuation from Forbes via YC page. Series C extension 20M at 1.1B reported by Axios (June 2025 per YC page) and a Business Wire release. Series D 200M at 2.15B per company release and Reuters. Series A and seed not found; funding is partial. onebrief.com fetch was blocked by a rate limited safety check and the Business Wire page returned 403. Aggregator totals conflict (73M to 320M). Competitor search found no 2021 dated sources, only later partner mentions, so the list is empty. Co-founders other than Grant Demaree not named on sources opened.
